name: Rome
operatingHours: Metro lines A, B/B1 and C run ~5:30 AM–11:30 PM, until ~1:30 AM on Friday and Saturday nights. No all-night metro; night buses (N lines) cover the gap. Strikes (usually announced Fridays) can shut lines for part of the day.
fareInfo: A BIT ticket costs €1.50 (2026) and is valid 100 minutes: one metro ride plus unlimited buses and trams. Tap a contactless bank card or phone at the gates to pay the same fare, capped at €8.50 a day. Passes: 24 h €8.50, 48 h €15, 72 h €22. City tickets do not cover the Leonardo Express (€14) to Fiumicino.

sights.name: Colosseum
sights.note: The 1st-century amphitheatre of Flavian Rome, once holding some 50,000 spectators for gladiator games; timed entry, with a separate ticket for the arena floor and underground.
sights.hours: 8:30 AM–6:30 PM until late Oct, 8:30 AM–4:30 PM in winter; last entry 1 h before close

sights.name: Pantheon
sights.note: Hadrian's 2,000-year-old temple, still crowned by the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome and its open oculus; now a church and Raphael's tomb.
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–7:00 PM daily (last entry 6:30 PM); €7 ticket

sights.name: Trevi Fountain
sights.note: Rome's grandest Baroque fountain, where a coin tossed over the shoulder promises a return trip; since Feb 2026 a €2 ticket is needed to step down to the basin edge.
sights.hours: Basin access 9:00 AM–10:00 PM (from 11:30 AM Mon & Fri), last entry 9:00 PM; piazza always open and free

sights.name: Trastevere
sights.note: Cobbled riverside quarter of ivy-draped lanes, trattorias and evening crowds, centred on Piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere and its mosaic-fronted basilica.

sights.name: Vatican Museums
sights.note: The papal collections, from classical sculpture to the Raphael Rooms, ending in Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel ceiling and Last Judgment.
sights.hours: Mon–Sat 8:00 AM–8:00 PM (last entry 6:00 PM); closed Sun except last Sun of month 9:00 AM–2:00 PM (free)

sights.name: Galleria Borghese
sights.note: A cardinal's villa packed with Bernini's marble sculptures and paintings by Caravaggio, Raphael and Titian, visited in strict two-hour slots.
sights.hours: Tue–Sun 9:00 AM–7:00 PM, entry on the hour; closed Mon; booking required

sights.name: Piazza Navona
sights.note: Long oval square on the footprint of Domitian's stadium, with Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers at its centre and street artists all around.

sights.name: Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore
sights.note: One of Rome's four major papal basilicas, with 5th-century mosaics, a gilded coffered ceiling and the tomb of Pope Francis; a short walk from Termini.

sights.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
sights.note: Hadrian's mausoleum turned papal fortress, linked to the Vatican by a walled passage, with a rooftop terrace looking straight down to St Peter's.

sights.name: Palatine Hill
sights.note: The hill where Rome's emperors built their palaces, now gardens and ruins with views over the Forum and the Circus Maximus; same ticket as the Colosseum.
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–6:30 PM until late Oct, 9:00 AM–4:30 PM in winter; last entry 1 h before close

sights.name: Villa Borghese
sights.note: Rome's central park of pines, a boating lake and the Pincio terrace overlooking Piazza del Popolo; rent a bike or rowing boat.
sights.hours: Park open 24 hours; Pincio and attractions daylight hours

sights.name: Roman Forum
sights.note: The heart of ancient Rome: temples, triumphal arches and the Senate house strung along the Via Sacra between the Capitoline and Palatine hills.
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–6:30 PM until late Oct, 9:00 AM–4:30 PM in winter; last entry 1 h before close

sights.name: Monumento a Vittorio Emanuele II
sights.note: The vast white marble 'Vittoriano' on Piazza Venezia, honouring Italy's first king; its terraces and paid glass lift give a 360° view of the city.
sights.hours: 9:30 AM–7:30 PM daily; panoramic lift extra

sights.name: Palazzo Colonna
sights.note: A princely family palace still in private hands, whose Great Hall of mirrors and frescoes rivals Versailles; opens to the public only a few mornings a week.
sights.hours: Sat 9:15 AM–1:15 PM; Fri mornings guided tours only (book); other days private tours

sights.name: Spanish Steps
sights.note: The 135-step Baroque stairway from Piazza di Spagna up to the Trinità dei Monti church; sitting on the steps is banned and fined.

sights.name: Chiesa di Sant'Ignazio di Loyola
sights.note: Jesuit church famous for Andrea Pozzo's illusionist ceiling and painted 'fake dome'; stand on the floor marker to see the trick work.

sights.name: St. Peter's Basilica
sights.note: The world's largest church, home to Michelangelo's Pietà and Bernini's bronze canopy; climb the dome for the classic view over St Peter's Square.
sights.hours: ~7:00 AM–8:00 PM daily (dome closes earlier); free with a security queue; may close during papal ceremonies

sights.name: Mercato di Testaccio
sights.note: A modern covered neighbourhood market with fruit stalls and much-loved street-food counters serving trapizzini and Roman sandwiches.

railStations.name: Roma Termini
railStations.note: Rome's main station and the only stop shared by metro lines A and B. Frecciarossa and Italo high-speed trains to Naples (~1h10), Florence (~1h30), Milan (~3h) and Venice (~4h); the Leonardo Express to Fiumicino Airport; airport buses to Ciampino.
railStations.hours: Station open ~4:30 AM–~1:30 AM. Mainline trains run to individual timetables.

railStations.name: Roma Tiburtina
railStations.note: Rome's second high-speed station (Frecciarossa and Italo, many northbound trains stop here instead of Termini), on metro line B. FL1 regional trains to Fiumicino Airport; the long-distance coach terminal is next door.
railStations.hours: Station open ~4:30 AM–~1:00 AM. Mainline trains run to individual timetables.

airports.name: Rome Fiumicino Airport
airports.transitNote: Leonardo Express non-stop to Roma Termini in ~32 min (€14; airport rail, not on this metro map). FL1 regional trains (€8) reach Trastevere and Tiburtina in ~30–50 min; coach buses to Termini ~50–70 min. Taxi fixed fare €55 to the historic centre.
airports.hours: Leonardo Express: first ~6:00 AM, last ~11:30 PM from the airport. Late arrivals: night buses or a taxi.

airports.name: Rome Ciampino Airport
airports.transitNote: No rail link: shuttle buses run to Roma Termini in ~40 min (~€6–7), or take a local bus to Ciampino station and a regional train to Termini (~15 min). The metro A stop Anagnina is a bus ride away. Taxi fixed fare €40 to the historic centre.
airports.hours: Airport shuttle buses: first ~4:30 AM, last ~midnight, timed to flights; check operator timetables.
